analysis.title: Is Hiding From AI Now The Most Crowded Trade Of All?
key_insights: Defensives in the US and Europe just closed their best monthly performance versus the market on record in October 2026. US consumer staples had their best month since October 2000.

Wilson (GS) says the AI axis has dominated market returns in 2026 and has crowded out other narratives. Even well diversified portfolios became more concentrated. He had written nearly 11 months ago that diversification was the price of staying fully invested.
The monthly return spread between the S&P ex-AI and the S&P swung from -6.4 points in April to +8.6 points in October, the two biggest readings in a decade of data.

The one-month correlation between the 10-year Treasury yield and AI-related equities rose to about 0.6, while the correlation with Brent, which drove yields for most of the Iran war, turned negative. When AI stocks fall, yields fall, because the bond market reads an AI selloff as a growth scare.
Wilson's principal components work says a meaningful amount of growth hit and policy tightening is already priced in, though the chart is a week out of date.

Miller's desk (GS custom baskets) says the rotation into defensives made sense as investors moved away from the AI pain trade, but valuations are now stretched. The US staples basket (GSXUSTAP) is up 19.8% versus the S&P on a rolling 22-day basis, the highest since at least 2014 and above the Covid spike.

GS Miller recommends going short US Staples (GSXUSTAP). Staples trade at their highest valuation premium to the SPX in 10+ years. The dividend yield is 200bps below the US 10Y and earnings growth does not justify the valuations.

Staples' forward dividend yield is about 2.05 points below the 10-year Treasury yield, the 1st percentile of its history relative to the 10-year. In 2020 staples paid more than two points over Treasuries.
After the nine previous months in which staples rallied more than 8%, the basket underperformed the S&P over the next three months seven times, by as much as 14.1 points.
European staples (GSXESTAP) yield 100bps more than US peers but have re-rated beyond earnings, at 16x earnings, the 90th percentile on a one-year view.

GS preferred expression is a dual binary paying if XLP falls and rates fall by mid-January: XLP below 97.5% of spot and the 10-year SOFR swap rate more than 15bps below the forward on January 15, 2027, for 14% of notional, roughly a 7x payout. It is cheap because the one-month correlation between XLP and 10-year yields is at -74%, near local lows.

Wilson says the pressure on consumer and rate-sensitive areas through 2026 has yet to reverse. YTD S&P sub-sectors: oil refiners +110%, household appliances -57%, auto parts -40%, footwear -36%, casinos -30%. He sees a catch-up case resting on a sharply higher cost of capital and inflationary pressure from higher energy costs.

Energy is easing: Brent is below $100, European gas (TTF) fell 17% on the week to about €86/MWh, and Iran is showing willingness to discuss nuclear issues previously off the table. GS European Hormuz Bottleneck basket (GSXEHRMZ) is up 30% since end of February but trades 25% rich to its five-year multiple, and consensus expects 75% of the basket to post falling earnings over two years.

October payrolls came in at 165K, more than double expectations, and put a December rate hike back on the table. That hurts the rate-sensitive catch-up trade and the rates-lower leg of the staples dual binary.

Wilson is optimistic: payrolls were robust, positioning has been hit, and rates and oil are easing. He is in the 1997/1998 camp rather than 1999/2000 and cites GS forecast of 18% EPS growth in 2027 and the 19/19 run for post mid-term equity rallies. Privorotsky (GS) took the same side on Friday.

The ZeroHedge author notes 1998's recovery came with three Fed cuts in seven weeks while 2026 faces a possible December hike. The author sides with Miller on staples and says the likeliest way staples lose their premium is an AI rebound sending hiders back, not a growth scare.
